issues.failure_explanation: The space of continuous piecewise tensor-product-degree-k functions on L cells does not have dimension Lk^d: continuity identifies the Lagrange nodes shared between adjacent cells. In 1D the dimension is Lk+1, not Lk (e.g., k=1 gives L+1 hat functions, not L). Moreover, taking k^d nodes per cell does not in general produce N=Lk^d distinct nodes, and interior-only nodes yield only bubble functions vanishing at cell interfaces, which do not span the stated space. The example is internally inconsistent, although the later order statement N=O((k/h)^d) remains correct.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the exact equality by the correct count (dimension equals the number of distinct Lagrange nodes, Theta(Lk^d)) or state only the order N=O((k/h)^d).
issues.overall_effect: Only the exact dimension/node count inside this illustrative example is wrong; the asymptotic order and the subsequent observation that empty cells make the empirical dictionary linearly dependent are unaffected.
issues.title: FEM example: wrong dimension and node count of the finite element space
issues.why_classification: Short local correction of an exact count that is used downstream only as a big-O statement; no claim, method, or guarantee changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The sentence claims Assumption moments assumption follows from Assumption assumption when X is compact. This is false: mu-a.e. continuity on a compact space does not imply boundedness. Counterexample: X=[0,1] with Lebesgue measure, psi = A psi = x^{-1/4}. Then psi is in L^2 and continuous a.e. (Assumption continuous holds), but psi*A psi = x^{-1/2} is not in L^2, so the moment assumption fails. One needs the functions to be bounded (e.g., continuous everywhere on the compact set, or in L^\infty).

issues.failure_explanation: With g = Psi(x) + eta one has E[g g^dagger] = G_N + E[eta eta^dagger], and E[eta eta^dagger] is a nonzero positive semidefinite matrix for any nondegenerate noise (e.g., sigma^2 Id for the Gaussian noise of Example noise example 1); likewise E[c c^dagger] = T_N + E[xi xi^dagger] and E[c g^dagger] = C_N + E[xi eta^dagger]. The quadratic noise terms are therefore not centered, so the summands S^G_m, S^C_m have nonzero mean and Bernstein's inequality (Theorem Bernstein theorem requires E[S_m]=0) is applied outside its hypotheses. The statement is in fact false: by the law of large numbers G-tilde_{NM} -> G_N + E[eta eta^dagger] a.s., so for delta < ||E[eta eta^dagger]|| the probability P[||G-tilde_{NM} - G_N|| < delta] tends to 0 as M grows, whereas the proposition asserts it is at least p for all sufficiently large M. There is an unavoidable noise-induced error floor at any fixed noise level.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either de-bias the empirical matrices using a known noise covariance (a new construction and a stronger assumption) or restate the bounds with an explicit bias/error-floor term of order ||E[eta eta^dagger]||*||G_N^{-1}||, thereby abandoning convergence at fixed noise level.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition noise bound and Theorem OC theorem noise (including (order of convergence noise)) are false at fixed noise level; the conclusion of Example noise example 1 that noise merely multiplies the bound by ~2 is unsupported; the prose claims that the framework 'accounts for the presence of noise' (abstract), that the error bounds extend 'to the case of noisy observations' (Contribution part 4), and that 'we again show convergence of the approximations to the true dynamics in this case' (end of Section 2) become unreliable.

issues.failure_explanation: The conditioning event E = {all M noise vectors bounded} has probability p-tilde_N^M (independence across m), not p-tilde_N. Hence p-tilde_N * P-tilde[A] = P[A cap E] / p-tilde_N^{M-1}, which is not <= P[A] in general (it already fails for A = E). The correct transfer is P[E] P-tilde[A] = P[A cap E] <= P[A], so the argument only yields the conclusion with probability p * p-tilde_N^{M-1}, which is exponentially small in M. Since the prescribed M grows like delta^{-2}, the requirement p-tilde_N^M > p needed by this strategy fails for large M, so the stated probability-(>= p) guarantee cannot be obtained by this argument.
